document.title: Automated SLA-driven Canary and Rollback Cookbook
document.content:
{
  "title": "Automated SLA-driven Canary and Rollback Cookbook",
  "space": "eng-private-deployments",
  "author": "Priya Nair",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-18",
  "last_updated": "2026-08-11",
  "reviewers": [
    "Evan Parker",
    "Lina G\u00f3mez",
    "Arjun Patel"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "canary",
    "rollback",
    "slo",
    "observability",
    "runbook"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/incremental-stateful-upgrade-strategy-2027",
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/steady-state-ops-and-cost-optimization-playbook-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "Summary:\\nThis cookbook defines an automated, SLA-driven canary strategy and corresponding rollback actions for private Redwood deployments (VPC and on-prem). It codifies signal aggregation, thresholds, and deterministic rollback sequencing so operators, SREs, and field engineers can run safe progressive rollouts and rely on automated protection when service-level objectives are violated.\\n\\nPurpose and scope:\\n- Purpose: Reduce human error during progressive rollouts by tying automated rollouts and rollbacks to observable SLAs and composite health signals.\\n- Scope: Applies to control-plane and model-serving releases for private deployments delivered via the Redwood operator (both VPC-managed and on-prem images). This document covers the canary policy, metric signals, decision logic, automated actions, manual escalation steps, and postmortem data collection.\\n\\nBackground:\\nMany incidents during upgrades are caused by subtle degradations (inference latency tails, increased token error rates, KV cache regressions) that are not visible from single metrics. Our approach combines multiple signals into a composite \\\"canary health score\\\" and enforces deterministic rollback/mitigation steps when score crosses configured thresholds.\\n\\nOwners and roles:\\n- Release owner: Product or Owner of the release (listed in release metadata).\\n- Canary executor (automation): eng-platform/canary-service (owned by the Runtime team).\\n- On-call SRE: eng-sre oncall rotation.\\n- Field operator: On-prem deployment engineer (customer-facing).\\n- Incident commander: assigned per incident matrix.\\n\\nHigh-level flow (summary):\\n1. Create canary release with metadata and small percentage routing (default 3%).\\n2. Start 30-minute observation window (configurable).\\n3. Collect signals (latency, error rate, quality evals, resource signals).\\n4. Calculate canary health score every 60s.\\n5. If score drops below yellow threshold -> partial mitigation (throttle, route to fallback model).\\n6. If score drops below red threshold or sustained degradation for X minutes -> automated rollback to previous model/release; notify stakeholders and create incident.\\n\\nCanary policy configuration (example YAML):\\n- policy_name: sla-driven-canary-2026\\n- rollout_percentages: [3, 10, 30, 70, 100]\\n- observation_window: 30m\\n- evaluation_interval: 60s\\n- thresholds:\\n  - green: score >= 0.90\\n  - yellow: 0.80 <= score < 0.90 (automated mitigation)\\n  - red: score < 0.80 (automated rollback)\\n- persistence: if any red occurs for >= 3 consecutive intervals -> rollback\\n\\nSample policy snippet (for operator):\\n---\\ncanary_policy:\\n  name: sla-driven-canary-2026\\n  rollout_steps: [3, 10, 30, 70, 100]\\n  observation_window: \\\"30m\\\"\\n  eval_interval: \\\"60s\\\"\\n  thresholds:\\n    green: 0.90\\n    yellow: 0.80\\n    red: 0.80\\n  rollforward_condition: \\\"all steps green for two consecutive windows\\\"\\n  rollback_condition: \\\"red for 3 consecutive intervals or sustained yellow for 4 intervals\\\"\\n---\\n\\nSignals used (metrics and derived signals):\\n1. latency_p95_ms (service: inference-runtime) \u2014 95th percentile latency in ms per request.\\n2. latency_p99_ms \u2014 99th percentile latency, used for tail SLOs.\\n3. token_error_rate \u2014 fraction of requests with generation truncation, EOS anomalies, or abrupt stream termination.\\n4. kv_cache_hit_rate \u2014 prefix cache hit rate; sudden drop indicates cache incompatibility or model mapping errors.\\n5. gpu_utilization_pct \u2014 GPU utilization at canary nodes (to detect OOM or kernel regressions).\\n6. model_quality_regressions_per_1k \u2014 automated eval harness detection of changed outputs for sampled prompt set (fuzzy match and semantic similarity).\\n7. infra_errors_per_min \u2014 kube or runtime-level errors per minute (OOMKills, PodRestarts, gRPC errors).\\n\\nComposite canary health score (algorithm):\\n- Each signal is normalized to [0,1] with directionality (higher is better). The weighted sum produces the health score.\\n- Default weights: latency_p95: 0.30, latency_p99: 0.20, token_error_rate: 0.20, kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.10, model_quality_regressions: 0.15, infra_errors: 0.05.\\n- Adjust weights per-release in release metadata when a rollout is known to be latency-sensitive vs. quality-sensitive.\\nFormula (described):\\nhealth_score = sum(weight_i * normalized(signal_i))\\nNormalization notes:\\n- latency normalized = 1 - min(1, (observed_p95 - baseline_p95) / p95_sla_margin)\\n- token_error normalized = 1 - token_error_rate / token_error_sla_limit\\n- kv_cache_hit normalized = min(1, kv_cache_hit_rate / baseline_cache_rate)\\n- model_quality normalized = 1 - (regressions_per_1k / regression_sla_limit)\\n\\nAutomated mitigation steps (yellow):\\n1. Limit new canary traffic increase (pause rollout).\\n2. Route subsequent requests for 50% of canary traffic to fallback model variant (model: <current>-compat).\\n3. Increase telemetry sampling (eval harness samples 10x more prompts for quality checks).\\n4. Notify on-call and release owner via the incident channel with auto-created ticket.\\n5. Continue to monitor for up to observation_window; if improved, reattempt rollout; if persists, escalate to rollback.\\n\\nAutomated rollback steps (red):\\n1. Immediately remove canary variant from load balancer (route 100% to previous stable model).\\n2. If model is part of a packaged image roll, mark rollout as failed and trigger automated image revert in orchestration.\\n3. Scale down canary nodes gracefully and drain with a 60s grace period.\\n4. Create a rollback incident with prepopulated logs, Grafana dashboards, and the last 60m of sampled generations attached.\\n5. Run an automated post-rollback validation (smoke tests) before closing the incident.\\n\\nManual rollback playbook (when automation is disabled or inconclusive):\\n1. Confirm degrade with metrics in the canary dashboard (last 30m). Check latency_p99, token_error_rate, and model_quality_regressions.\\n2. From operator workstation: run the rollback command:\\n   - redwoodctl rollout revert --deployment <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-version> --reason \\\"canary health score < 0.80\\\"\\n3. Verify routes: control-plane route list --deployment <deployment-id> (expect 100% -> previous).\\n4. Scale down canary nodes: kubectl -n redwood scale deployment <canary-depl> --replicas=0 (or use redwoodctl).\\n5. Wait for smoke tests: redwoodctl smoke --deployment <deployment-id> (must pass before incident closure).\\n\\nEscalation matrix and timelines:\\n- Automated rollback triggers incident at time T0.\\n- 0-10m: Automation runs rollback and posts to #prod-incidents; on-call SRE paged.\\n- 10-30m: On-call SRE validates rollback; if rollback fails or new symptoms appear, Incident Commander assigned.\\n- 30-120m: Field operator engaged if on-prem network/storage behavior suspected.\\n- >120m: Engage Release Manager and Customer Success for customer communications.\\n\\nObservability and dashboards (required panels):\\n- Canary overview: health_score time-series, rollout percentage, and detected flags.\\n- Per-metric panels: latency_p95, latency_p99, token_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate, model_quality_regressions, infra_errors_per_min.\\n- Trailing window traces: last 500 generations with similarity-score diffs to baseline.\\n- Smoke test result panel (pass/fail, timestamp).\\n\\nTelemetry retention and attachments (for postmortem):\\n- Attach last 60m of raw request/response pairs (sampling 1 in 50 by default).\\n- Attach all canary node kernel traces and GPU process logs for last 30m.\\n- Preserve model binaries and config hash for the failed canary version.\\n- Retention: 90 days for incident analysis; 366 days for legal/regulatory review (if customer requests).\\n\\nTesting and preflight checks (required before enabling auto-rollback):\\n- Baseline collection: gather 72h of baseline metrics for the target workload.\\n- Eval harness: run a 2k prompt consistency check with semantic similarity thresholding.\\n- Dry-run canary: simulate rollout with internal test traffic to validate health_score generation.\\n- Chaos test: spawn a controlled pod restart and ensure automated rollback behaves as expected.\\n\\nOperator quick commands (examples):\\n- Start canary: redwoodctl canary start --deployment <id> --policy sla-driven-canary-2026\\n- Pause rollout: redwoodctl canary pause --deployment <id>\\n- Force rollback: redwoodctl rollout revert --deployment <id> --to-version <stable-version> --force\\n- Fetch canary score: redwoodctl canary status --deployment <id> --last 10m\\n\\nPost-rollback triage checklist (first 24h):\\n1. Collect incident artifacts (logs, Grafana, traces).\\n2. Run root-cause hypotheses: regression in kernels, tokenizer changes, KV mapping mismatch, quantization incompatibility, operator config drift.\\n3. Run targeted tests: binary diff, tokenization sampling, KV cache warmup analysis.\\n4. If model-quality regressions found: roll model to compatibility variant and re-evaluate.\\n5. Produce a short RCA and action items within 3 business days.\\n\\nConfiguration table (reference values):\\n- Default rollout initial percentage: 3%\\n- Observation window: 30m\\n- Evaluation interval: 60s\\n- Yellow threshold (health_score): 0.80\\n- Red threshold (health_score): 0.80\\n- Consecutive red intervals to rollback: 3\\n- Sampling rate for attachments: 1/50 (adjustable per-customer)\\n\\nSecurity and customer privacy notes:\\n- Attachments are sanitized: we strip customer PII and redact prompt tokens flagged as sensitive before persistence.\\n- Access to incident artifacts is restricted to the release owner, eng-sre, and customer success for that account.\\n\\nAppendix A \u2014 Example incident timeline (realistic):\\n- 09:12: Canary started (3%)\\n- 09:42: health_score drops to 0.78 (2 consecutive intervals) -> automation applied mitigation (pause + fallback routing 50%).\\n- 09:50: score remains < 0.80 for 3 intervals -> automation triggers rollback at 09:50.\\n- 10:00: smoke tests pass; rollback incident created and marked resolved after RCA triage ticket opened.\\n\\nAppendix B \u2014 Quick validation checklist for field installs:\\n1. Ensure time sync (chrony/ntp) on all nodes.\\n2. Ensure telemetry agent version >= 2.4.1.\\n3. Ensure KMS connectivity for image signing checks.\\n4. Preload KV caches (if available) using the canonical warmup job.\\n5. Verify redwoodctl connectivity to control plane and operator permissions.\\n\\nReferences and related docs:\\n- Incremental stateful upgrade strategy (internal) \u2014 see related_pages\\n- Day-2 steady-state ops and cost optimization playbook \u2014 see related_pages\\n\\nContact and feedback:\\n- For questions about this cookbook, open a PR against this page or ping #runtime-canary (Slack).\\n- Suggested improvements: adjust weights per-application; standardize canary dashboards across customers.\\n\\nEnd of document.",
  "end": "",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],

}

{

    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/upgrade-prechecks-spec.json",
    "title": "Private Upgrades: Preflight (Precheck) Specification",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{
  "title": "Private Upgrades: Preflight (Precheck) Specification",
  "space": "eng-private-deployments",
  "author": "Ethan Park",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-04-18",
  "last_updated": "2025-06-07",
  "reviewers": [
    "Connor O'Brien",
    "Irene Choi",
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Marcus Lin",
    "Fatima Noor",
    "Sahana Iyer"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "private",
    "upgrades",
    "rollback",
    "installer",
    "prechecks",
    "onprem",
    "vpc",
    "reliability"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-upgrade-and-rollback-overview",
    "eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/backup-and-restore-strategy-private",
    "eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/rollback-semantics-and-hooks",
    "eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/onprem-upgrade-bundle-format",
    "policies-and-process/change-management/private-release-gating-and-change-management"
  ],
  "body": "## Purpose\nThis page specifies **preflight checks (\"prechecks\")** executed by `redwood-private-installer` before any Redwood Private upgrade steps are performed. The goal is to prevent common upgrade failures by validating environment readiness up front and producing **actionable remediation guidance**.\n\nThis spec covers:\n- Check categories and required inputs\n- Pass/fail criteria and thresholds\n- **Blocking vs warning** behavior\n- Standardized error codes, messages, and operator remediation\n- Special considerations for **VPC** vs **on-prem/air-gapped** deployments\n\nNon-goals:\n- Replacing runtime monitoring during upgrades (see SRE alert runbooks)\n- Full coverage for every historical migration edge case (installer will explicitly identify \"manual intervention required\")\n\n---\n\n## Definitions\n- **Private deployment**: Redwood Private control plane + data plane running in customer-controlled environment (VPC or on-prem).\n- **Precheck**: A deterministic validation executed before generating/executing an upgrade plan.\n- **Blocking**: Failure stops the upgrade and requires remediation.\n- **Warning**: Failure does not stop the upgrade, but is surfaced in output and stored in upgrade artifacts; operator must explicitly acknowledge for execution.\n- **Upgrade target**: The requested version(s) of Redwood Private components (installer, charts, platform control plane, data plane services).\n\n---\n\n## Operator Experience (CLI contract)\nPrechecks run as part of plan generation and can be invoked explicitly.\n\n### Commands\n- `redwood-private upgrade plan --to <version> [--bundle <path>] [--format json|table]`\n  - Runs prechecks by default\n  - Writes an auditable plan artifact that includes precheck results\n\n- `redwood-private upgrade precheck --to <version> [--bundle <path>] [--output <file>] [--fail-on-warn]`\n  - Runs only prechecks\n  - Does not mutate cluster state\n\n### Output requirements\n- Human-friendly table output for terminals\n- Structured JSON output for automation\n- Each check must provide:\n  - `id`, `title`, `severity`, `result` (PASS/WARN/FAIL/SKIP)\n  - `reason` (short)\n  - `details` (relevant values; redacted where sensitive)\n  - `remediation` (actionable steps)\n  - Optional `links` (internal docs + commonly used upstream docs)\n\n### Exit codes\n- `0`: all PASS (and WARN only if not using `--fail-on-warn`)\n- `2`: at least one WARN and `--fail-on-warn` enabled\n- `3`: at least one FAIL\n- `4`: execution error (unexpected exception, permissions, network issues that prevent checks from running)\n\n---\n\n## Severity model\nEach precheck has a **default severity** which determines behavior.\n\n| Severity | Behavior | Intended use |\n|---|---|---|\n| BLOCK | Upgrade cannot proceed (plan generation may proceed but execution must be blocked). | High probability of outage or irrecoverable partial upgrade (e.g., unsupported version jump, DB unreachable). |\n| WARN | Upgrade can proceed but requires explicit operator acknowledgement in plan/apply step. | Elevated risk or degraded experience (e.g., storage headroom near threshold, cert expiring soon). |\n| INFO | Informational only; never blocks. | Helpful context for operator (e.g., control plane latency). |\n\n### Acknowledgement rule\nIf any WARN checks are present, `upgrade apply` must require either:\n- `--ack-warnings`, or\n- a plan field `warnings_acknowledged_by` + `warnings_acknowledged_at` (set by the installer when applying with acknowledgement)\n\n---\n\n## Execution model\n### Ordering\nChecks execute in the following order to improve signal quality and reduce confusing cascades:\n1) Local environment + inputs (kubeconfig, bundle path)\n2) Kubernetes API connectivity + permissions\n3) Cluster health + capacity checks\n4) Storage + snapshot capability\n5) Control plane endpoints (DNS/TLS)\n6) Database connectivity + migration safety\n7) Artifact availability + integrity verification\n8) Compatibility / supported upgrade path gating\n\n### Mutability\nPrechecks must be **read-only**. The following are allowed:\n- API reads (Kubernetes API, DNS, HTTPS HEAD/GET, DB read-only probes)\n- Listing resources (pods, nodes, PVCs)\n- Creating ephemeral objects **only if explicitly marked** and cleaned up (preferred: avoid). Current policy: **no cluster writes** during prechecks.\n\n### Timeouts\nDefault per-check timeout: **20s**\n- Networking-related checks may use **60s** (DNS/TLS, artifact endpoints)\nOverall precheck budget: **5 minutes** (fail fast if BLOCK failures are found)\n\n### Redaction\n- Never print secrets, bearer tokens, client certs, or full connection strings.\n- DB endpoints may be printed; usernames may be printed; passwords must not.\n- Bundle paths are acceptable; bundle contents hashes are acceptable.\n\n---\n\n## Standard error format\nEach check must use:\n- **Stable error code**: `RWPRV-PRE-<category>-<number>`\n- Message should be actionable and reference the failing resource/value.\n\nExample:\n- Code: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-001`\n- Message: `Cannot connect to Postgres at <host>:<port> using configured secret redwood-postgres (timeout after 20s).`\n- Remediation:\n  1. `kubectl -n redwood-private get secret redwood-postgres -o yaml` (verify host/port/user)\n  2. Validate network policy allows egress to DB\n  3. Run `psql` from a debug pod in-cluster\n\n---\n\n## Check catalog (spec)\nThe following checks are required for GA. Each includes default severity, pass criteria, and remediation.\n\n### Category A: Inputs & environment\n\n#### A1. Kubeconfig present and usable\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-001`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **What it validates**: Installer can reach the Kubernetes API using provided kubeconfig/context.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Kubernetes API `/version` responds\n  - Current context resolves to a cluster\n- **Fail message**: `Unable to reach Kubernetes API using context <context>.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Verify `KUBECONFIG` and context: `kubectl config current-context`\n  - Verify cluster access: `kubectl get ns`\n  - For on-prem: ensure VPN/bastion connectivity to API server\n\n#### A2. Namespace exists\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-002`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Target namespace `redwood-private` (default) exists.\n- **Pass criteria**: Namespace exists.\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Create namespace or set correct namespace flag: `--namespace`\n\n#### A3. Installer/operator permissions (RBAC)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-003`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Caller has required permissions to read and later upgrade resources.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - `kubectl auth can-i` checks pass for:\n    - get/list/watch pods, deployments, sts, jobs, configmaps, secrets (read-only for precheck)\n    - get/list/watch pv/pvc/storageclasses\n    - get nodes (or equivalent via cluster role; if nodes are hidden, allow skip with warning and rely on metrics fallback)\n- **Fail message**: `Insufficient RBAC permissions to validate/upgrade resources in namespace <ns>.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Bind required ClusterRole/Role to installer principal.\n  - If using a ServiceAccount, ensure it has `view` + upgrade-specific permissions.\n\n---\n\n### Category B: Kubernetes cluster health & scheduling readiness\n\n#### B1. Cluster version supported\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-010`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Kubernetes version is in the supported matrix for the target Private version.\n- **Pass criteria**: `v1.<minor>` within supported range for `<target version>`.\n- **Fail message**: `Kubernetes <version> is not supported for target <target>.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Upgrade cluster to a supported Kubernetes minor version before upgrading Redwood Private.\n  - If customer cannot upgrade K8s, pin Redwood Private to a compatible version.\n\n#### B2. Node readiness\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-011`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Nodes are Ready and schedulable.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - 0 nodes in `NotReady`\n  - No control-plane taints that would prevent required jobs/pods (unless workloads are explicitly tolerated)\n- **Fail message**: `Cluster has <n> NotReady nodes; upgrade jobs may not schedule reliably.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Fix node health (cloud provider events, kubelet, disk pressure)\n  - Drain/replace unhealthy nodes\n\n#### B3. System pods health (kube-system)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-012`\n- **Severity**: WARN\n- **Validates**: Core components are stable to reduce upgrade flakiness.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - `coredns` pods Ready\n  - CNI pods Ready (vendor-specific)\n  - No crashlooping kube-system pods impacting DNS/network\n- **Warn message**: `Detected unhealthy kube-system pods (DNS/CNI). Upgrade may fail due to networking instability.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Resolve DNS/CNI issues; confirm name resolution in cluster\n\n#### B4. Redwood namespace baseline health\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-013`\n- **Severity**: WARN\n- **Validates**: Existing Redwood components are mostly healthy before upgrading.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - No more than 0 CrashLoopBackOff pods in `redwood-private`\n  - No Pending pods older than 10 minutes\n- **Warn message**: `Existing Redwood workloads are unhealthy; upgrading an unhealthy cluster increases rollback risk.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Investigate failing pods prior to upgrade: `kubectl -n redwood-private get pods` and `kubectl describe`\n  - Resolve image pull errors, quota, or config issues\n\n---\n\n### Category C: Resource capacity & quotas\n\n#### C1. CPU/memory headroom (best-effort)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-CAP-001`\n- **Severity**: WARN\n- **Validates**: There is enough headroom for temporary upgrade jobs and rolling updates.\n- **Pass criteria** (best-effort):\n  - At least 10% allocatable CPU and memory unrequested OR can schedule 1 additional small job (250m CPU, 512Mi) in namespace.\n- **Warn message**: `Cluster appears resource constrained; upgrade jobs may be evicted or fail to schedule.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Temporarily scale down non-critical workloads or add capacity.\n  - Ensure namespace quotas allow upgrade jobs.\n\n#### C2. Namespace resource quotas\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-CAP-002`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Namespace quotas will not prevent required jobs.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - If ResourceQuota exists: available limits for pods/jobs, CPU, memory, PVCs.\n- **Fail message**: `ResourceQuota in <ns> prevents upgrade job creation (pods/jobs quota exhausted).`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Increase quota or clean up completed jobs.\n\n---\n\n### Category D: Storage & snapshot readiness\n\n#### D1. Persistent volume usage headroom\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-STO-001`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: PVs used by Redwood control plane services (including Postgres if in-cluster) have sufficient free space.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - For each critical PVC: estimated free space >= **15%** OR >= **10GiB** (whichever is larger).\n  - If free-space cannot be measured reliably: require operator override and treat as WARN.\n- **Fail message**: `Insufficient storage headroom on PVC <pvc> (<free> free, requires >= <threshold>).`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Expand PVC (StorageClass must support expansion)\n  - Clean up logs/retention if applicable\n  - For on-prem: ensure backing storage has headroom and expansion workflow is validated\n\n#### D2. StorageClass supports snapshots or logical backup fallback configured\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-STO-002`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: A rollback-safe backup mechanism is available.\n- **Pass criteria** (one of):\n  - CSI VolumeSnapshot supported for PVCs that will be backed up, OR\n  - Logical DB backup configured and tested (Postgres dump), OR\n  - Cloud provider snapshot integration available (EBS snapshot for AWS-managed PVs)\n- **Fail message**: `No supported backup mechanism detected for rollback safety (snapshots not available and logical backup not configured).`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Install CSI snapshot controller and define VolumeSnapshotClass\n  - Enable logical backups in installer config\n  - Validate snapshot permissions (cloud IAM) for VPC deployments\n\n#### D3. Snapshot permission check (cloud/VPC)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-STO-003`\n- **Severity**: WARN\n- **Validates**: Snapshot APIs can be invoked by the environment (IAM/permissions), where applicable.\n- **Pass criteria**: Best-effort detection based on cloud environment and snapshot class presence.\n- **Warn message**: `Snapshot controller detected but permissions could not be verified; backup step may fail at runtime.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Confirm IAM permissions for snapshot creation\n  - Perform a test snapshot outside of upgrade window\n\n---\n\n### Category E: Database connectivity & migration safety\n\n#### E1. Postgres reachable\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-001`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Control plane DB endpoint is reachable from the cluster.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - TCP connect succeeds and DB responds to `SELECT 1` within 20s\n- **Fail message**: `Cannot connect to Postgres for control plane state (timeout/refused).`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Validate service endpoint/hostname\n  - Confirm NetworkPolicy/SG/firewall egress\n  - Confirm DB is running and accepting connections\n\n#### E2. DB credentials valid (least privilege)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-002`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Provided DB user can authenticate and has required privileges for migrations.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Authentication succeeds\n  - Required privileges present for schema migrations (as defined by Private DB role policy)\n- **Fail message**: `DB user lacks required privileges for schema migration.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Update role grants per DB policy\n  - Rotate credentials in Kubernetes secret\n\n#### E3. Migration lock availability\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-003`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Migration lock can be acquired and there is no concurrent migration.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Lock acquisition probe succeeds within 5s\n  - No active migration recorded in migrations table/state\n- **Fail message**: `Database migration lock is held; another migration may be running or a previous upgrade left a stale lock.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Confirm no other upgrade is in progress\n  - Follow runbook to clear stale lock (requires SRE approval)\n\n#### E4. DB version supported and parameters safe\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-004`\n- **Severity**: WARN\n- **Validates**: Postgres major/minor version supported and safe settings present.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Postgres major version in supported range\n  - `statement_timeout` and lock timeouts meet minimums recommended by Redwood migrations (or are unset)\n- **Warn message**: `Postgres version/settings may cause long locks or timeouts during migration.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Adjust timeouts per runbook\n  - Schedule longer maintenance window\n\n---\n\n### Category F: Identity, RBAC, and SSO reachability\n\n#### F1. OIDC/SSO endpoint reachable (if enabled)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-AUTH-001`\n- **Severity**: WARN\n- **Validates**: If OIDC is configured for Private Console/API auth, issuer is reachable and metadata can be fetched.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - HTTPS GET to `/.well-known/openid-configuration` succeeds\n- **Warn message**: `OIDC issuer is unreachable from cluster; users may not be able to sign in post-upgrade.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Validate DNS + egress rules to IdP\n  - For on-prem: ensure IdP is reachable from cluster network\n\n#### F2. ServiceAccount tokens and projected volume support\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-AUTH-002`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Cluster supports projected service account tokens used by newer components.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Kubernetes version supports bound service account tokens\n  - Feature gates not disabling required behavior\n- **Fail message**: `Cluster configuration does not support required ServiceAccount token projection for target version.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Update cluster configuration or pin to compatible version\n\n---\n\n### Category G: Networking, DNS, and TLS\n\n#### G1. Private control plane FQDN resolves in-cluster\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-NET-001`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: DNS resolution for configured endpoints used during upgrade and health verification.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - A/AAAA record resolves for `private.<customer-domain>` and any configured artifact mirrors\n- **Fail message**: `DNS resolution failed for <hostname> from cluster context.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Fix CoreDNS configuration\n  - Fix upstream DNS forwarding / split-horizon DNS\n  - For VPC: validate Route53 private hosted zone associations\n\n#### G2. TLS certificate validity and expiry window\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-NET-002`\n- **Severity**: WARN (BLOCK if already expired)\n- **Validates**: TLS certs used by console/API/control plane endpoints are valid.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Certificate chain validates (or matches configured trust bundle)\n  - Not expired\n  - Expiry >= **30 days** (else WARN)\n- **Warn message**: `TLS certificate for <hostname> expires in <days> days; upgrade window may overlap renewal.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Renew certificate before upgrade\n  - Ensure trust bundle is updated in cluster\n\n#### G3. Egress reachability to required endpoints\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-NET-003`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK (VPC/hosted artifacts), WARN (on-prem with offline bundle)\n- **Validates**: Cluster can reach required endpoints depending on installation mode:\n  - Online: container registry, chart repo, release metadata\n  - Offline: artifact mirror endpoints (if configured) or local bundle\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Online mode: HTTPS reachability to configured endpoints\n  - Offline mode: skip online checks if `--bundle` provided and verified\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Update firewall/proxy settings\n  - Configure `artifact_mirror_endpoint` (on-prem)\n  - Provide verified upgrade bundle\n\n---\n\n### Category H: Artifact availability and integrity\n\n#### H1. Target release metadata available\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-ART-001`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Installer can locate the target release manifest (versions, component images, chart versions).\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Online: release manifest fetched successfully\n  - Offline: release manifest present in bundle\n- **Fail message**: `Target release metadata for <target> not found (online fetch failed and no valid bundle provided).`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Check target version name\n  - Provide `--bundle` or configure mirror\n  - Validate proxy settings\n\n#### H2. Helm chart availability\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-ART-002`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Required charts can be pulled (or are present in the bundle).\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Chart refs resolve and are pullable\n- **Fail message**: `Unable to pull Helm chart <chart>@<version>.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Validate chart repo URL/mirror\n  - For air-gapped: ensure bundle contains chart tarballs and index\n\n#### H3. Container image availability (HEAD check)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-ART-003`\n- **Severity**: WARN (BLOCK if images are strictly required in offline mode and missing)\n- **Validates**: Image tags/digests exist in registry and are accessible.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - For each required image digest: registry responds and auth works\n- **Warn message**: `Some images could not be verified in registry; rollout may fail with ImagePullBackOff.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Validate registry credentials and permissions\n  - For on-prem: ensure offline registry mirror is synced\n\n#### H4. Offline bundle checksum/signature verification (on-prem)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-ART-004`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Air-gapped bundle integrity.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Manifest file present\n  - Checksums match\n  - Signature verifies against configured public key (if signature enforcement enabled)\n- **Fail message**: `Upgrade bundle failed integrity verification (checksum/signature mismatch).`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Re-download bundle from trusted source\n  - Verify transfer method preserves file integrity\n  - Confirm correct public key configured\n\n---\n\n### Category I: Compatibility policy (supported upgrade paths)\n\n#### I1. Supported upgrade path (N-1 \u2192 N)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-COMPAT-001`\n- **Severity**: BLOCK\n- **Validates**: Upgrade path complies with policy.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Default supported path: **N-1 \u2192 N** for the current major/minor train\n  - Installer version is compatible with target platform version\n- **Fail message**: `Unsupported upgrade path from <current> to <target>. Supported: N-1 \u2192 N.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Upgrade sequentially\n  - If customer requires a jump, engage Release Eng + SRE for a supervised plan\n\n#### I2. Mixed-version constraints (control plane vs data plane)\n- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-COMPAT-002`\n- **Severity**: WARN\n- **Validates**: Temporary mixed-version window is within allowed bounds.\n- **Pass criteria**:\n  - Control plane and data plane versions do not exceed allowed skew as defined in compatibility matrix\n- **Warn message**: `Planned upgrade may temporarily exceed recommended version skew; ensure maintenance window and rollback plan.`\n- **Remediation**:\n  - Use staged plan (control plane first, then data plane)\n  - Avoid pausing mid-upgrade\n\n---\n\n## Blocking vs Warning policy (summary)\nThe following checks are always **BLOCK** on failure:\n- Kubernetes API connectivity and namespace existence\n- RBAC required for upgrade operations\n- Supported Kubernetes version\n- Node readiness (hard failure)\n- Namespace quota prevents job/pod creation\n- Storage headroom below threshold\n- Backup mechanism not available\n- DB unreachable/invalid credentials/migration lock held\n- DNS failure for required hostnames (when those hostnames are required for health checks)\n- Target release metadata not available\n- Unsupported upgrade path\n- Offline bundle verification failure\n\nThe following are **WARN** by default:\n- kube-system instability (DNS/CNI)\n- Existing Redwood namespace unhealthy\n- General CPU/memory headroom\n- Snapshot permission uncertainty\n- Postgres version/timeout settings at risk\n- OIDC issuer reachability\n- TLS cert expiring soon\n- Image availability best-effort verification\n\nOwners may promote WARN \u2192 BLOCK for a specific release train via change-management gating (see related policy page).\n\n---\n\n## Remediation guidance style guide\nEach remediation section must:\n1) State the goal in plain language (\"Ensure DB is reachable from the cluster\")\n2) Provide 2\u20135 concrete commands or steps\n3) Call out when escalation is required (\"If you cannot clear locks safely, contact Redwood Support\")\n\n### Example remediation snippet template\n- **Confirm**: `kubectl -n redwood-private get pods`\n- **Inspect**: `kubectl -n redwood-private describe pod <pod>`\n- **Logs**: `kubectl -n redwood-private logs <pod> --tail=200`\n- **Fix**: (specific action)\n- **Re-run**: `redwood-private upgrade precheck --to <target>`\n\n---\n\n## Special considerations\n### On-prem / air-gapped\n- Network egress checks must not block if a valid offline bundle is provided and mirror endpoints are configured.\n- Bundle verification (`RWPRV-PRE-ART-004`) is mandatory and blocking.\n- DNS checks should validate internal artifact mirrors and internal control plane endpoints (not public endpoints).\n\n### VPC\n- Artifact endpoints are typically online; egress reachability (`RWPRV-PRE-NET-003`) is blocking unless an approved mirror/bundle workflow is used.\n- Snapshot permission checks should be enabled where cloud IAM integration is detectable.\n\n---\n\n## Auditability requirements\nPrecheck results must be persisted in the upgrade artifact and included in support bundles.\nMinimum fields to record:\n- Timestamp, installer version, current cluster version, current Private version, target version\n- Full precheck list with results and error codes\n- Warning acknowledgements (who/when)\n\nAdditionally, the platform must emit audit log events:\n- `private.upgrade.precheck.started`\n- `private.upgrade.precheck.completed` (include counts: pass/warn/fail)\n\n---\n\n## Appendix: Example JSON output (contract)\n(Shown as text for documentation purposes.)\n\n{\n  \"prechecks_version\": \"1\",\n  \"started_at\": \"2025-06-07T18:42:10Z\",\n  \"target_version\": \"private-2.18.0\",\n  \"results\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"RWPRV-PRE-DB-001\",\n      \"title\": \"Postgres reachable\",\n      \"severity\": \"BLOCK\",\n      \"result\": \"FAIL\",\n      \"reason\": \"timeout\",\n      \"details\": \"dial tcp <redacted-host>:5432 timed out after 20s\",\n      \"remediation\": \"Verify DB endpoint, network policies, and credentials; run SELECT 1 from a debug pod.\",\n      \"links\": \"eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/private-upgrade-runbook#db-connectivity\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n\n---\n\n## Change log\n- 2025-06-07: Updated storage headroom thresholds and added explicit bundle integrity BLOCK requirement for on-prem.\n- 2025-05-22: Added migration lock probe and standardized error codes.\n- 2025-04-18: Initial published version.",

{
  "title": "Private Upgrades: Preflight (Precheck) Specification",
  "space": "eng-private-deployments",
  "author": "Ethan Park",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2025-04-18",
  "last_updated": "2025-06-07",
  "reviewers": [
    "Connor O'Brien",
    "Irene Choi",
    "Sean Gallagher",
    "Marcus Lin",
    "Fatima Noor",
    "Sahana Iyer"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "private",
    "upgrades",
    "rollback",
    "installer",
    "prechecks",
    "onprem",
    "vpc",
    "reliability"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "related_pages": [
    "eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-upgrade-and-rollback-overview",
    "eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/backup-and-restore-strategy-private",
    "eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/rollback-semantics-and-hooks",
    "eng-private-deployments/onprem-packaging/onprem-upgrade-bundle-format",
    "policies-and-process/change-management/private-release-gating-and-change-management"
  ],
  "body": "## Purpose
This page specifies **preflight checks ("prechecks")** executed by `redwood-private-installer` before any Redwood Private upgrade steps are performed. The goal is to prevent common upgrade failures by validating environment readiness up front and producing **actionable remediation guidance**.

This spec covers:
- Check categories and required inputs
- Pass/fail criteria and thresholds
- **Blocking vs warning** behavior
- Standardized error codes, messages, and operator remediation
- Special considerations for **VPC** vs **on-prem/air-gapped** deployments

Non-goals:
- Replacing runtime monitoring during upgrades (see SRE alert runbooks)
- Full coverage for every historical migration edge case (installer will explicitly identify "manual intervention required")

---

## Definitions
- **Private deployment**: Redwood Private control plane + data plane running in customer-controlled environment (VPC or on-prem).
- **Precheck**: A deterministic validation executed before generating/executing an upgrade plan.
- **Blocking**: Failure stops the upgrade and requires remediation.
- **Warning**: Failure does not stop the upgrade, but is surfaced in output and stored in upgrade artifacts; operator must explicitly acknowledge for execution.
- **Upgrade target**: The requested version(s) of Redwood Private components (installer, charts, platform control plane, data plane services).

---

## Operator Experience (CLI contract)
Prechecks run as part of plan generation and can be invoked explicitly.

### Commands
- `redwood-private upgrade plan --to <version> [--bundle <path>] [--format json|table]`
  - Runs prechecks by default
  - Writes an auditable plan artifact that includes precheck results

- `redwood-private upgrade precheck --to <version> [--bundle <path>] [--output <file>] [--fail-on-warn]`
  - Runs only prechecks
  - Does not mutate cluster state

### Output requirements
- Human-friendly table output for terminals
- Structured JSON output for automation
- Each check must provide:
  - `id`, `title`, `severity`, `result` (PASS/WARN/FAIL/SKIP)
  - `reason` (short)
  - `details` (relevant values; redacted where sensitive)
  - `remediation` (actionable steps)
  - Optional `links` (internal docs + commonly used upstream docs)

### Exit codes
- `0`: all PASS (and WARN only if not using `--fail-on-warn`)
- `2`: at least one WARN and `--fail-on-warn` enabled
- `3`: at least one FAIL
- `4`: execution error (unexpected exception, permissions, network issues that prevent checks from running)

---

## Severity model
Each precheck has a **default severity** which determines behavior.

| Severity | Behavior | Intended use |
|---|---|---|
| BLOCK | Upgrade cannot proceed (plan generation may proceed but execution must be blocked). | High probability of outage or irrecoverable partial upgrade (e.g., unsupported version jump, DB unreachable). |
| WARN | Upgrade can proceed but requires explicit operator acknowledgement in plan/apply step. | Elevated risk or degraded experience (e.g., storage headroom near threshold, cert expiring soon). |
| INFO | Informational only; never blocks. | Helpful context for operator (e.g., control plane latency). |

### Acknowledgement rule
If any WARN checks are present, `upgrade apply` must require either:
- `--ack-warnings`, or
- a plan field `warnings_acknowledged_by` + `warnings_acknowledged_at` (set by the installer when applying with acknowledgement)

---

## Execution model
### Ordering
Checks execute in the following order to improve signal quality and reduce confusing cascades:
1) Local environment + inputs (kubeconfig, bundle path)
2) Kubernetes API connectivity + permissions
3) Cluster health + capacity checks
4) Storage + snapshot capability
5) Control plane endpoints (DNS/TLS)
6) Database connectivity + migration safety
7) Artifact availability + integrity verification
8) Compatibility / supported upgrade path gating

### Mutability
Prechecks must be **read-only**. The following are allowed:
- API reads (Kubernetes API, DNS, HTTPS HEAD/GET, DB read-only probes)
- Listing resources (pods, nodes, PVCs)
- Creating ephemeral objects **only if explicitly marked** and cleaned up (preferred: avoid). Current policy: **no cluster writes** during prechecks.

### Timeouts
Default per-check timeout: **20s**
- Networking-related checks may use **60s** (DNS/TLS, artifact endpoints)
Overall precheck budget: **5 minutes** (fail fast if BLOCK failures are found)

### Redaction
- Never print secrets, bearer tokens, client certs, or full connection strings.
- DB endpoints may be printed; usernames may be printed; passwords must not.
- Bundle paths are acceptable; bundle contents hashes are acceptable.

---

## Standard error format
Each check must use:
- **Stable error code**: `RWPRV-PRE-<category>-<number>`
- Message should be actionable and reference the failing resource/value.

Example:
- Code: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-001`
- Message: `Cannot connect to Postgres at <host>:<port> using configured secret redwood-postgres (timeout after 20s).`
- Remediation:
  1. `kubectl -n redwood-private get secret redwood-postgres -o yaml` (verify host/port/user)
  2. Validate network policy allows egress to DB
  3. Run `psql` from a debug pod in-cluster

---

## Check catalog (spec)
The following checks are required for GA. Each includes default severity, pass criteria, and remediation.

### Category A: Inputs & environment

#### A1. Kubeconfig present and usable
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-001`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **What it validates**: Installer can reach the Kubernetes API using provided kubeconfig/context.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Kubernetes API `/version` responds
  - Current context resolves to a cluster
- **Fail message**: `Unable to reach Kubernetes API using context <context>.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Verify `KUBECONFIG` and context: `kubectl config current-context`
  - Verify cluster access: `kubectl get ns`
  - For on-prem: ensure VPN/bastion connectivity to API server

#### A2. Namespace exists
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-002`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Target namespace `redwood-private` (default) exists.
- **Pass criteria**: Namespace exists.
- **Remediation**:
  - Create namespace or set correct namespace flag: `--namespace`

#### A3. Installer/operator permissions (RBAC)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-003`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Caller has required permissions to read and later upgrade resources.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - `kubectl auth can-i` checks pass for:
    - get/list/watch pods, deployments, sts, jobs, configmaps, secrets (read-only for precheck)
    - get/list/watch pv/pvc/storageclasses
    - get nodes (or equivalent via cluster role; if nodes are hidden, allow skip with warning and rely on metrics fallback)
- **Fail message**: `Insufficient RBAC permissions to validate/upgrade resources in namespace <ns>.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Bind required ClusterRole/Role to installer principal.
  - If using a ServiceAccount, ensure it has `view` + upgrade-specific permissions.

---

### Category B: Kubernetes cluster health & scheduling readiness

#### B1. Cluster version supported
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-010`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Kubernetes version is in the supported matrix for the target Private version.
- **Pass criteria**: `v1.<minor>` within supported range for `<target version>`.
- **Fail message**: `Kubernetes <version> is not supported for target <target>.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Upgrade cluster to a supported Kubernetes minor version before upgrading Redwood Private.
  - If customer cannot upgrade K8s, pin Redwood Private to a compatible version.

#### B2. Node readiness
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-011`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Nodes are Ready and schedulable.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - 0 nodes in `NotReady`
  - No control-plane taints that would prevent required jobs/pods (unless workloads are explicitly tolerated)
- **Fail message**: `Cluster has <n> NotReady nodes; upgrade jobs may not schedule reliably.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Fix node health (cloud provider events, kubelet, disk pressure)
  - Drain/replace unhealthy nodes

#### B3. System pods health (kube-system)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-012`
- **Severity**: WARN
- **Validates**: Core components are stable to reduce upgrade flakiness.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - `coredns` pods Ready
  - CNI pods Ready (vendor-specific)
  - No crashlooping kube-system pods impacting DNS/network
- **Warn message**: `Detected unhealthy kube-system pods (DNS/CNI). Upgrade may fail due to networking instability.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Resolve DNS/CNI issues; confirm name resolution in cluster

#### B4. Redwood namespace baseline health
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-K8S-013`
- **Severity**: WARN
- **Validates**: Existing Redwood components are mostly healthy before upgrading.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - No more than 0 CrashLoopBackOff pods in `redwood-private`
  - No Pending pods older than 10 minutes
- **Warn message**: `Existing Redwood workloads are unhealthy; upgrading an unhealthy cluster increases rollback risk.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Investigate failing pods prior to upgrade: `kubectl -n redwood-private get pods` and `kubectl describe`
  - Resolve image pull errors, quota, or config issues

---

### Category C: Resource capacity & quotas

#### C1. CPU/memory headroom (best-effort)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-CAP-001`
- **Severity**: WARN
- **Validates**: There is enough headroom for temporary upgrade jobs and rolling updates.
- **Pass criteria** (best-effort):
  - At least 10% allocatable CPU and memory unrequested OR can schedule 1 additional small job (250m CPU, 512Mi) in namespace.
- **Warn message**: `Cluster appears resource constrained; upgrade jobs may be evicted or fail to schedule.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Temporarily scale down non-critical workloads or add capacity.
  - Ensure namespace quotas allow upgrade jobs.

#### C2. Namespace resource quotas
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-CAP-002`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Namespace quotas will not prevent required jobs.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - If ResourceQuota exists: available limits for pods/jobs, CPU, memory, PVCs.
- **Fail message**: `ResourceQuota in <ns> prevents upgrade job creation (pods/jobs quota exhausted).`
- **Remediation**:
  - Increase quota or clean up completed jobs.

---

### Category D: Storage & snapshot readiness

#### D1. Persistent volume usage headroom
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-STO-001`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: PVs used by Redwood control plane services (including Postgres if in-cluster) have sufficient free space.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - For each critical PVC: estimated free space >= **15%** OR >= **10GiB** (whichever is larger).
  - If free-space cannot be measured reliably: require operator override and treat as WARN.
- **Fail message**: `Insufficient storage headroom on PVC <pvc> (<free> free, requires >= <threshold>).`
- **Remediation**:
  - Expand PVC (StorageClass must support expansion)
  - Clean up logs/retention if applicable
  - For on-prem: ensure backing storage has headroom and expansion workflow is validated

#### D2. StorageClass supports snapshots or logical backup fallback configured
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-STO-002`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: A rollback-safe backup mechanism is available.
- **Pass criteria** (one of):
  - CSI VolumeSnapshot supported for PVCs that will be backed up, OR
  - Logical DB backup configured and tested (Postgres dump), OR
  - Cloud provider snapshot integration available (EBS snapshot for AWS-managed PVs)
- **Fail message**: `No supported backup mechanism detected for rollback safety (snapshots not available and logical backup not configured).`
- **Remediation**:
  - Install CSI snapshot controller and define VolumeSnapshotClass
  - Enable logical backups in installer config
  - Validate snapshot permissions (cloud IAM) for VPC deployments

#### D3. Snapshot permission check (cloud/VPC)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-STO-003`
- **Severity**: WARN
- **Validates**: Snapshot APIs can be invoked by the environment (IAM/permissions), where applicable.
- **Pass criteria**: Best-effort detection based on cloud environment and snapshot class presence.
- **Warn message**: `Snapshot controller detected but permissions could not be verified; backup step may fail at runtime.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Confirm IAM permissions for snapshot creation
  - Perform a test snapshot outside of upgrade window

---

### Category E: Database connectivity & migration safety

#### E1. Postgres reachable
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-001`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Control plane DB endpoint is reachable from the cluster.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - TCP connect succeeds and DB responds to `SELECT 1` within 20s
- **Fail message**: `Cannot connect to Postgres for control plane state (timeout/refused).`
- **Remediation**:
  - Validate service endpoint/hostname
  - Confirm NetworkPolicy/SG/firewall egress
  - Confirm DB is running and accepting connections

#### E2. DB credentials valid (least privilege)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-002`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Provided DB user can authenticate and has required privileges for migrations.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Authentication succeeds
  - Required privileges present for schema migrations (as defined by Private DB role policy)
- **Fail message**: `DB user lacks required privileges for schema migration.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Update role grants per DB policy
  - Rotate credentials in Kubernetes secret

#### E3. Migration lock availability
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-003`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Migration lock can be acquired and there is no concurrent migration.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Lock acquisition probe succeeds within 5s
  - No active migration recorded in migrations table/state
- **Fail message**: `Database migration lock is held; another migration may be running or a previous upgrade left a stale lock.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Confirm no other upgrade is in progress
  - Follow runbook to clear stale lock (requires SRE approval)

#### E4. DB version supported and parameters safe
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-DB-004`
- **Severity**: WARN
- **Validates**: Postgres major/minor version supported and safe settings present.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Postgres major version in supported range
  - `statement_timeout` and lock timeouts meet minimums recommended by Redwood migrations (or are unset)
- **Warn message**: `Postgres version/settings may cause long locks or timeouts during migration.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Adjust timeouts per runbook
  - Schedule longer maintenance window

---

### Category F: Identity, RBAC, and SSO reachability

#### F1. OIDC/SSO endpoint reachable (if enabled)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-AUTH-001`
- **Severity**: WARN
- **Validates**: If OIDC is configured for Private Console/API auth, issuer is reachable and metadata can be fetched.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - HTTPS GET to `/.well-known/openid-configuration` succeeds
- **Warn message**: `OIDC issuer is unreachable from cluster; users may not be able to sign in post-upgrade.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Validate DNS + egress rules to IdP
  - For on-prem: ensure IdP is reachable from cluster network

#### F2. ServiceAccount tokens and projected volume support
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-AUTH-002`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Cluster supports projected service account tokens used by newer components.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Kubernetes version supports bound service account tokens
  - Feature gates not disabling required behavior
- **Fail message**: `Cluster configuration does not support required ServiceAccount token projection for target version.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Update cluster configuration or pin to compatible version

---

### Category G: Networking, DNS, and TLS

#### G1. Private control plane FQDN resolves in-cluster
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-NET-001`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: DNS resolution for configured endpoints used during upgrade and health verification.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - A/AAAA record resolves for `private.<customer-domain>` and any configured artifact mirrors
- **Fail message**: `DNS resolution failed for <hostname> from cluster context.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Fix CoreDNS configuration
  - Fix upstream DNS forwarding / split-horizon DNS
  - For VPC: validate Route53 private hosted zone associations

#### G2. TLS certificate validity and expiry window
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-NET-002`
- **Severity**: WARN (BLOCK if already expired)
- **Validates**: TLS certs used by console/API/control plane endpoints are valid.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Certificate chain validates (or matches configured trust bundle)
  - Not expired
  - Expiry >= **30 days** (else WARN)
- **Warn message**: `TLS certificate for <hostname> expires in <days> days; upgrade window may overlap renewal.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Renew certificate before upgrade
  - Ensure trust bundle is updated in cluster

#### G3. Egress reachability to required endpoints
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-NET-003`
- **Severity**: BLOCK (VPC/hosted artifacts), WARN (on-prem with offline bundle)
- **Validates**: Cluster can reach required endpoints depending on installation mode:
  - Online: container registry, chart repo, release metadata
  - Offline: artifact mirror endpoints (if configured) or local bundle
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Online mode: HTTPS reachability to configured endpoints
  - Offline mode: skip online checks if `--bundle` provided and verified
- **Remediation**:
  - Update firewall/proxy settings
  - Configure `artifact_mirror_endpoint` (on-prem)
  - Provide verified upgrade bundle

---

### Category H: Artifact availability and integrity

#### H1. Target release metadata available
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-ART-001`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Installer can locate the target release manifest (versions, component images, chart versions).
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Online: release manifest fetched successfully
  - Offline: release manifest present in bundle
- **Fail message**: `Target release metadata for <target> not found (online fetch failed and no valid bundle provided).`
- **Remediation**:
  - Check target version name
  - Provide `--bundle` or configure mirror
  - Validate proxy settings

#### H2. Helm chart availability
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-ART-002`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Required charts can be pulled (or are present in the bundle).
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Chart refs resolve and are pullable
- **Fail message**: `Unable to pull Helm chart <chart>@<version>.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Validate chart repo URL/mirror
  - For air-gapped: ensure bundle contains chart tarballs and index

#### H3. Container image availability (HEAD check)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-ART-003`
- **Severity**: WARN (BLOCK if images are strictly required in offline mode and missing)
- **Validates**: Image tags/digests exist in registry and are accessible.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - For each required image digest: registry responds and auth works
- **Warn message**: `Some images could not be verified in registry; rollout may fail with ImagePullBackOff.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Validate registry credentials and permissions
  - For on-prem: ensure offline registry mirror is synced

#### H4. Offline bundle checksum/signature verification (on-prem)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-ART-004`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Air-gapped bundle integrity.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Manifest file present
  - Checksums match
  - Signature verifies against configured public key (if signature enforcement enabled)
- **Fail message**: `Upgrade bundle failed integrity verification (checksum/signature mismatch).`
- **Remediation**:
  - Re-download bundle from trusted source
  - Verify transfer method preserves file integrity
  - Confirm correct public key configured

---

### Category I: Compatibility policy (supported upgrade paths)

#### I1. Supported upgrade path (N-1 → N)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-COMPAT-001`
- **Severity**: BLOCK
- **Validates**: Upgrade path complies with policy.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Default supported path: **N-1 → N** for the current major/minor train
  - Installer version is compatible with target platform version
- **Fail message**: `Unsupported upgrade path from <current> to <target>. Supported: N-1 → N.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Upgrade sequentially
  - If customer requires a jump, engage Release Eng + SRE for a supervised plan

#### I2. Mixed-version constraints (control plane vs data plane)
- **ID**: `RWPRV-PRE-COMPAT-002`
- **Severity**: WARN
- **Validates**: Temporary mixed-version window is within allowed bounds.
- **Pass criteria**:
  - Control plane and data plane versions do not exceed allowed skew as defined in compatibility matrix
- **Warn message**: `Planned upgrade may temporarily exceed recommended version skew; ensure maintenance window and rollback plan.`
- **Remediation**:
  - Use staged plan (control plane first, then data plane)
  - Avoid pausing mid-upgrade

---

## Blocking vs Warning policy (summary)
The following checks are always **BLOCK** on failure:
- Kubernetes API connectivity and namespace existence
- RBAC required for upgrade operations
- Supported Kubernetes version
- Node readiness (hard failure)
- Namespace quota prevents job/pod creation
- Storage headroom below threshold
- Backup mechanism not available
- DB unreachable/invalid credentials/migration lock held
- DNS failure for required hostnames (when those hostnames are required for health checks)
- Target release metadata not available
- Unsupported upgrade path
- Offline bundle verification failure

The following are **WARN** by default:
- kube-system instability (DNS/CNI)
- Existing Redwood namespace unhealthy
- General CPU/memory headroom
- Snapshot permission uncertainty
- Postgres version/timeout settings at risk
- OIDC issuer reachability
- TLS cert expiring soon
- Image availability best-effort verification

Owners may promote WARN → BLOCK for a specific release train via change-management gating (see related policy page).

---

## Remediation guidance style guide
Each remediation section must:
1) State the goal in plain language ("Ensure DB is reachable from the cluster")
2) Provide 2–5 concrete commands or steps
3) Call out when escalation is required ("If you cannot clear locks safely, contact Redwood Support")

### Example remediation snippet template
- **Confirm**: `kubectl -n redwood-private get pods`
- **Inspect**: `kubectl -n redwood-private describe pod <pod>`
- **Logs**: `kubectl -n redwood-private logs <pod> --tail=200`
- **Fix**: (specific action)
- **Re-run**: `redwood-private upgrade precheck --to <target>`

---

## Special considerations
### On-prem / air-gapped
- Network egress checks must not block if a valid offline bundle is provided and mirror endpoints are configured.
- Bundle verification (`RWPRV-PRE-ART-004`) is mandatory and blocking.
- DNS checks should validate internal artifact mirrors and internal control plane endpoints (not public endpoints).

### VPC
- Artifact endpoints are typically online; egress reachability (`RWPRV-PRE-NET-003`) is blocking unless an approved mirror/bundle workflow is used.
- Snapshot permission checks should be enabled where cloud IAM integration is detectable.

---

## Auditability requirements
Precheck results must be persisted in the upgrade artifact and included in support bundles.
Minimum fields to record:
- Timestamp, installer version, current cluster version, current Private version, target version
- Full precheck list with results and error codes
- Warning acknowledgements (who/when)

Additionally, the platform must emit audit log events:
- `private.upgrade.precheck.started`
- `private.upgrade.precheck.completed` (include counts: pass/warn/fail)

---

## Appendix: Example JSON output (contract)
(Shown as text for documentation purposes.)

{
  "prechecks_version": "1",
  "started_at": "2025-06-07T18:42:10Z",
  "target_version": "private-2.18.0",
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "RWPRV-PRE-DB-001",
      "title": "Postgres reachable",
      "severity": "BLOCK",
      "result": "FAIL",
      "reason": "timeout",
      "details": "dial tcp <redacted-host>:5432 timed out after 20s",
      "remediation": "Verify DB endpoint, network policies, and credentials; run SELECT 1 from a debug pod.",
      "links": "eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/private-upgrade-runbook#db-connectivity"
    }
  ]
}

---

## Change log

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_f6d2378cbce14122993a3905aa091f14",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-consistency-chaos-validation-and-rollback-matrix-2028.json",
    "title": "KV cache consistency: chaos-validation and rollback matrix",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"KV cache consistency: chaos-validation and rollback matrix\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-private-deployments\",\n  \"author\": \"Asha Patel\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-11-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2027-01-09\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Liu Zhang\",\n    \"Nora Kaplan\",\n    \"Samir Rao\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"kv-cache\",\n    \"chaos-testing\",\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"private-deploy\",\n    \"day2\",\n    \"validation-matrix\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook-2025.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/incremental-stateful-upgrade-strategy-2027.json\",\n    \"sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/tenant-bootstrapping-and-immutable-upgrade-playbook-2026.json\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"Summary\\n=======\\nThis document defines a focused validation and rollback matrix for KV (key-value) cache state consistency in Redwood private deployments. It is intended for operator teams validating upgrades, runtime changes (quantization, kernel swaps), and chaos experiments that touch cache topology or eviction behavior. The goal is to provide repeatable checks, acceptance criteria, and a clear rollback decision matrix so customer-facing Private deployments maintain correctness and SLOs during day-2 activities.\\n\\nScope\\n-----\\n- Applies to Redwood Private control plane + runtime instances that use the distributed KV cache (local LRU + tiered remote backing).\\n- Covers: cache population/eviction, hot-swap of model shards, cross-node cache invalidation, and forced eviction/GC scenarios.\\n- Out of scope: upstream model weights distribution and hardware firmware issues (see hardware EOL docs).\\n\\nOwners and responsibilities\\n---------------------------\\n- Runbook owner: eng-private-deployments -> Day-2 Ops (on-call rotation).\\n- Primary validation engineer: named in run execution tickets (must be an SRE or runtime engineer).\\n- Customer communication: Account Success + Solutions Engineering for production-facing tests.\\n- Rollback authority: On-call SE + PM for the affected customer.\\n\\nPrerequisites and testbed configuration\\n--------------------------------------\\n1) A staging cluster that mirrors the customer's tenant topology (same VM/GPU mix, same KV shard counts).\\n2) Traffic generator: our workload-replay harness (versioned) with 7-day sample of request distribution.\\n3) Telemetry collection: fine-grained sampling of kv.op.latency, kv.miss_rate, kv.consistency_violations, model.token-latency per route.\\n4) SLO baseline snapshot: capture 72-hour pre-test baseline for latency P50/P90/P99 and error_rate.\\n\\nValidation matrix (high level)\\n-----------------------------\\nThis matrix maps scenario -> validation steps -> automated guardrails -> rollback triggers.\\n\\n| Scenario | Core validation steps | Guardrail metrics (auto) | Rollback trigger (immediate) | Notes |\\n|---|---|---:|---|---|\\n| Node eviction (planned) | 1) Drain node; 2) Observe KV rebalancer; 3) Verify cache hot-keys rehydrate within 2x baseline cold-start | kv.miss_rate increase <= 3x baseline for <= 10m; kv.rebalance_errors == 0 | kv.rebalance_errors > 0 for 2m OR sustained kv.miss_rate > 3x baseline for 15m | Simulate with --evict-delay=30s to emulate graceful drain |\\n| Forced eviction (stress) | 1) Trigger eviction pressure; 2) Monitor per-tenant tail-latency and decode error counts; 3) Run consistency validator for sample request ids | model.tail_latency P99 increase <= 1.5x baseline; consistency_violations == 0 | any consistency_violations > 0 OR sustained P99 > 2x baseline for 10m | Run in blue/green canary ring first |\\n| Cross-node invalidation bug | 1) Introduce invalidation race via concurrent write tests; 2) Run deterministic replay; 3) Check idempotency and KV read-after-write | read_after_write_success_rate >= 99.99% | read_after_write_success_rate < 99.9% OR more than 1 data-mismatch in 100k ops | Use small blast radius and assert end-to-end hash checksums |\\n| Model shard hot-swap | 1) Swap model shard binary; 2) Check KV shard affinity and cached embeddings validity; 3) Run 1k query golden set | embedding_mismatch_count == 0; kv.miss_rate acceptable | embedding_mismatch_count > 0 OR error_rate increase > 0.5% sustained | Prefer staged swap with canary traffic (5%) |\\n\\nValidation steps (detailed)\\n--------------------------\\n1. Baseline capture (pre-test window):\\n   - Capture metrics for 72 hours: latency P50/P90/P99, token-throughput, kv.miss_rate, kv.hit_latency, kv.rebalance_time.\\n   - Create a baseline artifact (JSON) and attach to the test run ticket.\\n\\n2. Canary (ringed) execution:\\n   - Select 5% of tenant traffic in the staging cluster.\\n   - Run the scenario for a 20\\u201330 minute burn-in while collecting full telemetry.\\n   - Run the deterministic replay tool against canary nodes and run the consistency checker.\\n\\n3. Full run (if canary succeeds):\\n   - Execute global change during maintenance window.\\n   - Keep mitigation toggles ready: auto-evacuation-disabled, kv-rebalancer-throttle=0.2, eviction-pressure-safety=true.\\n\\nAutomated guardrails and alerting rules\\n--------------------------------------\\n- kv.consistency_violations: alert - critical when count >= 1 for 1m in production tenant rings.\\n- kv.rebalance_errors: alert - page on >= 1 in 2m during rebalances.\\n- model.tail_latency.p99: warn at 1.5x baseline, critical at 2x baseline.\\n- Auto-fallback job: if kv.rebalance_errors triggered, system will prevent next stage rollout and open rollback ticket (auto-created).\\n\\nRollback matrix (decision tree)\\n------------------------------\\n- If consistency_violations detected: immediate rollback of the change that modified cache topology or invalidation semantics. Steps:\\n  1) Pause routing to changed nodes (traffic manager -> weight=0).\\n  2) Revert config / restore previous runtime artifact.\\n  3) Run fast-integrity-scan (checksums on 1M sampled kv keys).\\n  4) If checksums pass, progressively re-enable traffic at 10/30/60 minute increments.\\n  5) If checksums fail, escalate to on-call runtime lead and open SE/Customer incident.\\n\\n- If sustained latency degradation without data mismatches: roll forward mitigation (throttle rebalancer, increase cache size) for hot fix; only rollback if mitigation fails within 30m.\\n\\nRunbook: executing a validation run (operator steps)\\n--------------------------------------------------\\n1. Create a run ticket in JIRA project PRIV-RUN with tags: kv-cache, chaos-validation, <customer-id>.\\n2. Attach baseline artifact and planned scenario script.\\n3. Perform canary run and annotate observations in the ticket.\\n4. If canary passes, schedule full run during maintenance window and notify stakeholders (30m/10m/5m warnings).\\n5. Execute full run and keep the rollback playbook open in parallel.\\n\\nAcceptance criteria (pass/fail)\\n------------------------------\\n- Pass if:\\n  - No consistency_violations observed during canary and full run.\\n  - model.tail_latency.p99 increase <= 1.5x baseline for <= 30 minutes after change.\\n  - kv.rebalance_errors remain == 0.\\n- Fail if any consistency_violations occur or if automated rollback triggers fire.\\n\\nTelemetry and sampling guidance\\n------------------------------\\n- Sampling rate: kv.operation_trace sample=1/1000 by default; increase to 1/100 for any validation run.\\n- Mandatory logs to collect: kv.op.trace (json), cache-shard-metrics.csv (1s rollups), node-procstats (30s).\\n- Attach generated trace artifacts to the JIRA ticket; preserve for 90 days for postmortem analysis.\\n\\nCLI and example commands\\n------------------------\\n- Start a canary with the replay harness:\\n  ./replay --tenant <tenant-id> --ratio 0.05 --trace-sampling 0.01 --scenario kv-invalidation-race --output run-<date>.json\\n\\n- Trigger a forced eviction (staging only):\\n  redwood-admin evict --shard <shard-id> --pressure 0.9 --duration 300s\\n\\n- Run the integrity checksum utility (sampled):\\n  ./kv-checksum --cluster staging --sample 100000 --output checksum-<date>.ndjson\\n\\nAppendix: common failure patterns and mitigations\\n------------------------------------------------\\n- Pattern: slow rehydrate after drain -> Mitigation: pre-warm hot-key loader and increase kv.rebalance_window to 60s.\\n- Pattern: transient read-after-write mismatch under high-write bursts -> Mitigation: apply write-ack serialisation window or enable stronger consistency mode for affected tenant.\\n- Pattern: configuration drift between nodes -> Mitigation: run node-config-compare across cluster and auto-fix drifted keys.\\n\\nReferences\\n----------\\n- See runtime state migration playbook: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/kv-cache-migrations-and-runtime-state-migration-playbook-2025.json\\n- Incremental upgrade guidance: sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/incremental-stateful-upgrade-strategy-2027.json\\n\\nChange history\\n--------------\\n- 2026-11-15: Created by Asha Patel (initial draft).\\n- 2026-12-08: Added automated guardrail thresholds and CLI examples (reviewer Liu Zhang).\\n- 2027-01-09: Finalized rollback runbook and sampling guidance (published).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_f6d2378cbce14122993a3905aa091f14\"\n}",
